title: Own the per-project task-sync opt-in setting in Engram
outcome: Own the per-project task-sync opt-in setting in Engram
acceptance: Engram owns a per-project task-sync opt-in setting with explicit, attributed enable and disable actions through the Engram CLI and MCP; TermAl reads and writes it only through that supported Engram API; no TermAl-owned or Git-admin file holds it, and nothing infers it from shared or Git files (Greg's correction relayed by Engram::Advisor, 2026-10-12 #1280).

The setting is off by default and fails closed: an absent setting reads as disabled with reason "not configured (off by default)", and an invalid or unreadable one reads as unknown with its reason; both gate as not enabled.

A dedicated non-strict status read reports format engram-task-sync-status-v1, project_id, state enabled, disabled or unknown (never implied by absence), reason, and a one-line effect description; fail-first tests cover absent, invalid, disabled and enabled.
Its storage location is presented to Greg and decided before code when it changes the durable store; TermAl's three strict readers are not changed.

completion.summary: Engram owns per-project task-sync status/enable/disable through shared CLI and MCP service, with attributed explicit enable, off-by-default and fail-closed reads, private atomic file replacement and no SQLite or strict-reader changes. Validated and landed.
